subject: Post-call: pricing targets & host benchmarking for token economics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: pricing targets & host benchmarking for token economics

Hi Alice — thanks for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on economics and timing.

Recap (from our notes):
- Expected monthly token consumption: 120M input + 360M output = ~480M tokens/mo (aggregate prod + inference cache hit assumptions).
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + triage assistant (latency SLO: p95 < 450ms).
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a hard target in procurement of $6–8 / 1M tokens for run-time inference (post-quantization) to meet budget for Y1.
- Current host costs (what you’re seeing today): OpenAI equivalent ~ $18 / 1M tokens (chat 8k-class), Anthropic-hosted ~ $14 / 1M, other self-hosted/open-host providers range $9–12 / 1M depending on commitment and quantization.

Attached: high-level cost model (redwood_token_cost_model_v1.xlsx) with scenarios for 50–500M tokens. I put a conservative baseline and two aggressive cases (dedicated + 12mo commit; on-prem with custom quantization).

Benchmarks (back-of-envelope):
- OpenAI (hosted): ~$18 / 1M tokens (observed for similar prompt mixes).
- Anthropic-hosted: ~$14 / 1M.
- Open-model hosts (managed): $9–12 / 1M (wide variance on infra mix & model family).
- Redwood hosted (proposed): $10.5 / 1M standard, $7.5 / 1M with dedicated reserved capacity + 12mo commit (estimates only; final depends on model selection and KV-cache hit rate).

Questions / asks (next steps):
1) Can procurement confirm whether $6–8 / 1M is a strict cap or a preferred range? If strict, we’ll model a dedicated + aggressive quantization path and surface tradeoffs on latency/quality.
2) Would you share the procurement template or pricing constraints (Procurement contact copied)? We’ll prepare a short two-page pricing annex and a canary rollout plan.
3) Are there any compliance constraints that push you to Private (VPC/on-prem)? That materially changes unit costs.

Suggested next meeting: 30 min pricing deep-dive with procurement + engineering — availability Wed/Thu this week?

Thanks — I’ll prep the quick scenarios and share before the call.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_token_cost_model_v1.xlsx (excel)]

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing targets & host benchmarking for token economics

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap and the model. A few clarifications from procurement:

- The $6–8 / 1M is our preferred target for operating costs across the production workload. $6 is a stretch but acceptable if we can demonstrate parity on latency and a measurable quality delta (tiny regression tolerance).
- Compliance: for initial rollout we prefer our data stay in a VPC; on-prem is an option but adds procurement friction.
- Timeline: pilot (10–20M tokens/mo) in Q3, production (450–500M tokens/mo) by Q1 next year.

Procurement asked for two things before the pricing call:
1) A conservative/realistic scenario that hits $6.0 / 1M — list of tradeoffs (e.g., model family change, 4-bit quantization, increased cache hit assumptions, reserved capacity length).
2) An alternative that meets $8.0 / 1M with minimal quality impact (preferred initial ask).

I’m available Thu 29 Apr 09:00–11:00 ET or Fri 30 Apr 13:00–16:00 ET for a short call.

–Alice
Director, Product 
Acme Health

On Sun, Apr 25, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (See above)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing targets & host benchmarking for token economics

Hi Alice / team — thanks for the clear ask. I ran three concrete scenarios against the numbers you provided and attached a short slide with the delta assumptions (also exported as PDF): acme_requirements_draft.pdf. Short summary below.

Scenario A — Aggressive (target $6.00 / 1M)
- Approach: Dedicated Redwood Private (VPC) deployment + 4-bit quantization on select model layers + 12mo commitment + 70% KV/prefix cache hit assumed.
- Expected: ~$6.0 / 1M tokens (latency: p95 projected 420–480ms; small QoR risk on edge-case hallucinations, we recommend a narrow eval suite).
- Tradeoffs: Higher engineering integration, longer procurement lead time, add-on for KMS/HSM.

Scenario B — Balanced (target $8.00 / 1M)
- Approach: Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity (shared infra but reserved), 8-bit quantization, 12mo commit, conservative 50% cache hit.
- Expected: ~$7.8 / 1M tokens; latency p95 < 350ms; low quality regression risk.
- Tradeoffs: Moderate commit, quicker to pilot.

Scenario C — Low friction (baseline hosted)
- Approach: Redwood hosted with token-volume discount at 480M/mo band.
- Expected: ~$10.5 / 1M tokens; fastest time-to-value; no infra changes.

Competitive frame vs hosts (summary):
- OpenAI: ~$18 / 1M (hosted chat pricing equivalence we observed for similar workloads).
- Anthropic-hosted: ~$14 / 1M.
- Managed open-model hosts: $9–12 / 1M (depending on model family and optimized kernels).

Recommendation: If procurement can accept the VPC constraint and 12mo reserve, Scenario B is the fast path to hit your $8 target with minimal quality tradeoffs. Scenario A is possible but we should run a narrow QA prompt set and a short canary to validate quality.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm Thu 29 09:00 ET for a 30min pricing + procurement call (you gave earlier availability).
- I’ll bring Marissa (commercial lead) to table the contract/commit terms and Sean for technical latency/quantization detail.
- Pre-read: I’ll upload the short pricing annex to the HubSpot deal and drop the Drive link here before the call.

Thanks — I’ll schedule once Alice confirms a slot.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
